title: agent-login refuses a sandbox named with its group, so it cannot log in a sandbox outside the default group
foundBy: user report (host): agent-login failed on a sandbox in a named group on build 3d3fbb666359, confirmed against main by reading the command
details:
**What was seen.** This is what it prints for a sandbox in a group other than `default`:

```console
$ cs-sandbox agent-login claude <name>.<group>
cs-sandbox: launching cs-claude inside <name>.<group> — follow the prompts, then exit.
cs-sandbox: invalid sandbox name "<name>.<group>": use letters, digits and dashes only (must start and end alphanumeric)
```

The bare name resolves only in `default`, and fails with `no such sandbox "<name>" in group "default"; it exists as <name>.<group> — name the group`. The command has no flag for the group. So `agent-login` cannot reach any sandbox outside `default`. `cs-sandbox exec <name>.<group>` accepts the same reference.

**Why.** `newAgentLoginCmd` in `internal/cli/misc_commands.go` resolves the reference with `app.engineFor(name)` and then passes the unresolved `name` to `e.Exec`. The engine validates it as a bare sandbox name and refuses the dot. `exec` passes `in.Name`, the resolved instance's own name, and works.

**Why it matters.** SPEC section 10.1 names `agent-login` as the route for a sandbox that needs a login of its own. It is also how a person replaces an inherited login that has stopped working. The launch line printed before the failure also reads as though the login had started.

**Workaround.** Run `cs-sandbox exec <name>.<group>`, start the agent's CLI there, and log in by hand.

**What would help.** Pass `in.Name` to `Exec`, as `exec` does, and add `agent-login` to the table of commands tested with a group-qualified reference.
